subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw permit group chats to share an agent’s private main session, and must that opt-in be limited to explicit peer/binding allowlists rather than a global all-groups switch?
rationale: This changes the confidentiality and prompt-influence boundary between one-to-one and multi-party conversations; source inspection cannot determine the acceptable product trust model.

options.title: Explicit trusted-group bindings
options.body: Allow main-session routing only for individually matched group peers or bindings, with isolation remaining the default for all other groups.

options.title: Global group policy too
options.body: Also allow an account-wide group default, accepting that operators must understand it affects every matching group.

options.title: Keep isolation only
options.body: Reject shared main sessions for groups and direct users toward separate group contexts or explicit cross-session tooling.

recommendation.title: Explicit trusted-group bindings
recommendation.body: Allow main-session routing only for individually matched group peers or bindings, with isolation remaining the default for all other groups.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent routing and session-documentation history most directly covers the policy surface and its user-facing contract.
